reading:
Figure Ground has been judged twice in the main tournament. In round 10 it scored 6.41 (#13 of 19, in two judges' top fours, 5 promise votes; today's page scored 4.29). In round 11 it fell to 5.85 because nothing had changed. Its crossover child, Blueprint Terminal (6.71), put its colours onto a lit glass column.

WHAT THE JUDGES LOVE. The system judge called it "the most rigorous new system" of its round (style 7.7, interaction 7.7, type 7.1). Every part is a plate led by a figure drawn from the page's own data. The same figures are named again and again as worth keeping:
- Status's wiring of keys and connections, with lit ports
- To do's due queue with a NOW line
- the late tally by person
- the kinds tally
- the setup rungs
- the Settings machine, keyed 1-9 to its list

The graphics panel counted the wiring and the late bars among the best pictures of the round. Also praised:
- the strongest "here" in the squint (the reverse cell)
- the only To do page that marks LATE
- the lamp legend on Status
- underlined links
- a big Plex Sans Condensed title
- FIG captions and numbered sections (type)
- the tube's roll-on power-up

WHAT SANK IT, most cited first. None of these faults is in the idea itself.
1. Tracked mono caps on everything you press or follow: SEND, ALL PLANS, EDIT, COMPLETE, OR SNOOZE, 01 HOME. Type, system, interaction, usability and skeptic, in both rounds.
2. The paper-grey reverse cells. They are the brightest thing on the page that is not green, which is the glare the owner asked to lose (skeptic, feedback, soul; style and system in round 11).
3. No light. The greeting's lit glass pool is gone, and the figures are unlit blueprint drawings. Soul gave 5 and 5.4 ("flat and ruled rather than lit", "there is little tube light outside the radar").
4. Every row title is a blue underlined link. Judges said it reads as raw HTML, "a 1990s docs page".
5. Home runs to 2437px, with To do below the first screen, and has 14 targets under 44px (20 on To do).
6. The phone tabs are text only.
7. "CHAPTER 3 / FIG 1.2" read as costume and as noise to read past.
8. Smaller faults: ISO dates on To do, an italic caption, decorative figures (Home's family tree repeats the counts; the Plans key), a desktop chat that loses mine-versus-hers, and the radar eating Ideas' first phone screen.
9. The mood is "clever and cool rather than warm".

The later rounds' lessons still apply:
- Light is a list.
- A lit thing must draw live data, and no lit glass is empty.
- Late is shown in amber words.
- One control per filter.
- A head row with its one primary.
- State is shown by shape as well as colour.
- A change must be visible at page scale.

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT WIN. Keep the rule and fix every fault:
- Plex controls in sentence case.
- A "here" that does not glare.
- 0 small targets.
- Home near 1600px, with To do on the first screen.
- The greeting back in a lit pool.
- In each figure, only the live mark in full phosphor with the kit's two-layer halo: the NOW line, the working ports, the newest arrow, the step you are on. The rest of the drawing stays matte blueprint on a grounded slate drawing sheet.

Then the manual reads as lit, not printed. What would lift it further is tying each figure to its rows, so the drawing and the words read as one thing.

briefs.name: Lit Manual
briefs.hypothesis: The judges ranked the idea highly (system called it the most rigorous new system of its round; style and interaction 7.7, type 7.1). It lost on faults that are all fixable: caps, glare, no light, links that read as raw HTML, length, small targets and costume. Soul (5) and skeptic (6.2) marked it lowest, for the unlit greeting and the paper glare. Usability and interaction marked it down for targets, length and text-only tabs. This refinement fixes each of those without touching the idea. It also turns the drawings from printed to lit: one phosphor mark per figure, at the kit's full strength, the rest matte. That keeps the lenses that already liked it and lifts the ones that sank it. It should move from 6.41 into the upper 7s, and it gives the tour a design whose rules would hold on every page.
briefs.brief:
Start from r10-wild-4. Copy variants/r10-wild-4 (sheet.css and templates) to the new id and keep it a clean sheet. Keep the plate grammar: a rule across the top, the FIGURE in the left column on its drawing sheet, the words on the right, and a 1px hairline running down between them. Figures are drawn from the page's own data in blueprint line. Change what the judges named, and light each figure's live mark.

SYSTEM (every page)

1. Grid.
- At 64rem and up: `.plate { grid-template-columns: 16.5rem 1px minmax(0,1fr); column-gap: 2rem }`. The figure column was 19.5rem.
- `.fig { align-self: start; position: sticky; top: calc(var(--bar-h) + 1.5rem) }`. A long list keeps its drawing in view, and a short one leaves no gap under it.
- A plate with no data figure becomes `.plate.no-fig`, with one column spanning. This is the parent's own rule 7, now applied. The pictogram-on-a-sheet fillers (`.fig-picto`) go.

2. Grounded colour.
- Keep bg #0b100d.
- Ink warms to bone. This is the warm companion style asked for, put in the ink rather than in a paper fill:
  - --ink #dcd8ca (about 12.5:1)
  - --heading #e8e2d0
  - --ink-2 #b9b7ab
  - --dim #9a9d94
  - --faint #878b83
- The companion lives in one solid with a job: the DRAWING SHEET, `--sheet: #0f161c` (slate with a breath of blue).
  - Grid: rgb(159 180 214 / .07) every 12px, rgb(159 180 214 / .12) every 48px.
  - A 1px #26313a edge, and the parent's corner ticks.
  - Every figure on every page sits on it, so grounded colour runs down the left of every page.
- Drawing line `--draw: #6f88b3` at 1.25px (the old 1px lines were too thin at 100%). Figure labels `--draw-2: #9fb4d6`.
- Links: `--accent: #9fb4d6`, the quieter blueprint, replacing periwinkle #94bbfe.
- "Here" is a STEEL REVERSE cell. It replaces --paper #d4d4c9 everywhere: the bar, the List/Month and All ideas/Restaurants tabs, the Settings parts list and the phone tab.
  - `--here: #6e8496`, with a 2px #a9c4d8 cap along its top edge.
  - Text #0b100d, 4.9:1.
- Amber (--people #f1af64) keeps one job: late and needs a look.
- Family slips: `--slip: #1b2126`, with 1px #4c5760.
- Plate rules: 2px #56615d. This replaces the 3px #8d8f86 paper rule, which was the second-brightest grey on the page.

3. Type: one written scale in tokens, in the Plex superfamily.
- --t-title: 3rem/1.05, Plex Sans Condensed 600, -0.015em. Page titles and Home's question.
- --t-head: 1.75rem/1.15, Plex Sans Condensed 600. Plate heads.
- --t-lede: 1.125rem/1.5.
- --t-body: 1rem/1.5, Plex Sans.
- --t-small: .9375rem/1.45. Facts, help, captions.
- --t-fig: .875rem, Plex Mono 500, tabular-nums and "zero". Dates, times, counts and #ids only.
- --t-legend: .75rem, Plex Mono 500, caps, .04em. Figure legends, column heads and eyebrows only.
- Everything you press or follow is Plex Sans 600 .9375rem, sentence case: buttons, nav, tabs, disclosures and see-more links. No mono caps on any control.
- No italic anywhere (the figcaption italic goes).
- Measures: lede 58ch, chat 62ch.
- `text-wrap: balance` on heads, `pretty` on paragraphs.

4. Numbering.
- Drop the CHAPTER n eyebrow, the 01-10 numerals in the bar, and the 1.2 plate numbers in heads.
- Each figure keeps its number in a sentence-case caption under the sheet: "Fig. 2" in Plex Sans 600 --t-small --draw-2, then a short name ("This fortnight").

5. Links and rows.
- Row titles: --ink, Plex Sans 600, not underlined at rest. Underline (1px --accent, offset 3px) on :hover and :focus-visible.
- Head links ("All plans", "All 4", "All the setup steps") and links in prose stay underlined --accent, sentence case, with the right-arrow icon.

6. Controls.
- Every target is 44px or more:
  - `.section-head a`
  - `.tick`: a 1.25rem box in a 2.75rem hit square, pulled back into the line with negative margins
  - tabs, month-nav and starters (min-height 2.75rem, gap .5rem)
  - phone tabs, 3.5rem
- One primary per view. `.send` and `button.primary` in #6dff9c with #08120c text, square, with the kit's E3 ring and pool:
  - rest: `0 0 0 1px rgb(109 255 156/.35), 0 8px 28px -10px rgb(109 255 156/.7)`
  - hover: .5 / .85
  - fades on 1.2s cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.3,1)
- Secondaries (Filter, Cancel, Earlier, Later): a 1px --edge frame and ink text, no glow.
- Fields: filled boxes (#0f1412, 1px #515b56), 2.75rem tall, with E4 focus: phosphor edge, 3px ring at .16, 22px bloom, green caret, fading over 1.2s.
- Focus everywhere is E5: 2px #6dff9c, 3px offset. The parent's heavy double-rule focus goes. Add explicit rings for `input[type=checkbox]:focus-visible` and `select:open`.

7. Light, where the phosphor is (phosphor_kit.md). The kit's effects:
- E2 on the mark: tile, halo, icon drop-shadow, and a cursor that blinks 8 times then stays lit.
- E6 top haze under the bar.
- E1 two-layer halo on the question's key word.
- E3 on the one primary. E4 on the box being typed in.
- E12-E17 on the monitors at full strength: screen #6dff9c, bloom, .35px blur, scanlines, sheen, falloff, radar sweep with blips and afterglow, power light.
  - Cases are thin: a 3px graphite bezel #262c29, a 1px #3a423e lip, 10px outer radius. No slab.
  - Each tube is sized to its words; no empty glass.
- E16 power-on from a line on load, starting at opacity .05.
- E20 lamps on Status: a lit disc with 8px and 18px halos, breathing 3.2s.

The heart of this refinement: in every figure, ONE live mark is lit in phosphor, and everything else stays matte blueprint.
- `.d-live { stroke: #6dff9c; filter: drop-shadow(0 0 2px rgb(109 255 156/.8)) drop-shadow(0 0 7px rgb(109 255 156/.35)) }`
- `.d-lamp`: a #e4fff0 core in a brand halo.
- The live marks: the NOW line, today, the working ports and the live wire, the newest arrow, the step you are on, the part you are editing.

Row afterglow that shows in a still: a 12% steel wash (rgb(110 132 150/.12)) and a 2px inset sage edge (#86d9a6) on the left, on in .12s, fading over 1.2s.

Carry the kit's reduced-motion, more-contrast and forced-colours blocks.

PAGES

HOME (about 1600px at 1280, To do on the first screen)

Plate 1, the greeting, sits in a lit glass pool that spans both columns.
- `.plate.welcome` on #0f1512.
- E7's radial (70% 90% at 0% 100%, brand .13), plus `::before` scanlines (white 2.8%, 1px in 4) masked to the pool.
- A whisper of blueprint top right: radial 45% 70% at 100% 0%, rgb(159 180 214/.05).
- Its figure is the Next up monitor, moved up from Coming up. The family-tree figure goes, because it repeated the counts.
  - Thin case, radar with sweep, NEXT UP in inverse, "Pho Oregon", "Tuesday 29 September, 17:00 [TODAY]".
  - "> 4 more on the radar" with the block cursor, nowrap on the link text.
  - The pool rises from under the tube, so the monitor lights the box beside it.
- Words, in order:
  - the speaker line: her screen (E19), "Vera", the date in --t-small, nowrap
  - the question as the h1: --t-title, clamp(2rem, 1.2rem + 3.2vw, 3rem)
  - the ask box, full width, 3 rows, with E4's resting halo: border 38% brand into --line-2, glow 0 0 38px -20px brand/.6
  - one row: From select, Send where I am, mic, and Send (the page's one primary)
  - the starters as 44px sentence-case keys with 8px gaps
  - her last line, then "Continue with Vera"

Plate 2, at 80rem and up: "Coming up" and "To do" side by side in the words column (1.1fr | 1fr, gap 2rem), sharing one figure.
- Fig. 2, "This fortnight": a vertical time axis on the sheet.
  - The NOW line is lit; it is the one live mark.
  - Plans are numbered blueprint circles left of the axis, at their day.
  - Things due are squares right of it: late ones filled amber above NOW, dated ones hollow below, undated ones at the foot.
  - Numbers are keyed to the rows: stop 2 is Coming up's second row, #4 is the dentist.
  - Place stops by `entry.relative` where it parses (today 0, tomorrow 1, "in N days", "in N weeks" x7), otherwise in order.
- Coming up rows are ONE line, 48px: "Thu 1 Oct" (--t-fig, weekday dim) | the title (ink 600) | "10:00" | "in 2 days", right-aligned. A dotted leader only before the facts.
- To do rows: tick | title | owner | due in words. A late task says "was due 2 days ago" in amber, and its tick box is framed amber (L255).
- Below 80rem the two plates stack.

Plate 3: "Finish setting up" beside "The kids' wishes", spanning (no-fig). This folds figure 1.4 into the list.
- Each setup step is a 48px row: an amber-ringed numeral on a 1px blueprint line that ends in a hollow "Ready" stop.
- Amber is only an edge and a ring, never a fill. Neutral slate, no olive tray.
- Wishes: one line per kid, the name as a link and "0 open" in tabular figures.

Plate 4: "Lately added", spanning. The newest/the-rest squares figure goes.
- One-line rows: a kind square with the kind word (--t-legend), the title (ink), who it is for, and "#1" tabular at the right.
- "Something to eat" is its last row.
- "Add an idea" and "All 12" are underlined sentence-case links in the head.

CHAT

One plate.
- The figure column holds the sequence diagram, Fig. 1 "Who said what", sticky.
  - Her lit glyph screen (E19) heads her lifeline, and the newest arrow is the live mark.
  - The head's lonely glyph sheet goes.
  - Lifelines: Vera on the left, the family on the right.
- The transcript is laid out the same way.
  - Vera's lines sit on the bare glass at the left, with her screen.
  - The family's lines are steel slips (--slip, 1px #4c5760, a 3px #9fb4d6 edge on the right), right-aligned at 80% max. Their initial square is --slip with a bone letter, not paper.
- The date appears once, as a divider ("Sunday 27 September"). Each time ("19:48") sits at its line in --t-fig.
- The 01-04 numbers stay, dim, as the keys to the arrows.
- The composer sits at the foot, with Send as the primary.

IDEAS

Head plate.
- Figure: the radar map, thin-cased and lit, home at the hub, 16.5rem.
- Under the sheet: the nearest and furthest lines, with nowrap on "[18 MIN NW]". The reading note moves into the figcaption, not in italic.
- Words: title, lede, and "Add an idea" as the primary on the title's row.

List plate.
- The figure is the kinds tally, rebuilt in HTML as a control: 44px rows, each with a kind square, the kind word, a --draw bar, and the count in tabular figures.
  - Each row links to the list filtered by that kind; the current one is in steel reverse.
  - The Kind select is removed, so there is one control per filter.
- Filters on one row: Search (minmax(14rem,1.6fr)), Status, For, and Filter as a secondary.
- Rows are one line: "#1" | kind | title (ink) | "about 27 min S" | for.
- Phone: the radar drops to 7rem beside the nearest and furthest words.

PLANS

Head: title, lede, the source note, and List/Month as a latched pair of keys in steel, sentence case, with icons.
- No figure: the decorative legend key goes.

Month: the plate spans both columns.
- Today is a steel cell with a 6px lit E20 lamp in its corner. It is no longer amber, so amber keeps one job.
- Weekends are shaded with --sheet at 60%. Days from other months are hatched in --line.
- Plans in cells are ink titles, underlined on hover, with mono times.
- Earlier and Later are sentence-case secondaries, 44px.

List view.
- Figure: Fig. 1 "The next four weeks", Home's axis with plans only and NOW lit.
- Rows are one line, as on Home.

TO DO

Head: title and lede, with "Add something to do" as the primary on the title row (it opens the form).
- Figure: the late tally by person (kept). Its legend is squares: Late, Due, No date.

List plate.
- Figure: the due queue (kept). Its NOW line is lit and runs out of the sheet, across the hairline, into the list as a lit NOW divider between the late rows and the rest. Here the figure and the ground meet.
- Rows:
  - the tick, 44px, framed amber when late
  - "#4", dim
  - the title, ink 600
  - the owner
  - due in words, never ISO. A late task reads "Late · was due 2 days ago" in amber words; otherwise "due Thu 1 Oct, 19:56". Format it in the template from the fields the parent used, or reuse the Home row's words.
  - "No active reminder", small and dim
  - "Edit, complete or snooze" as a sentence-case disclosure with a pencil icon, 44px
- Show, Search and Filter on one line.

STATUS

Head.
- Figure: the wiring diagram (kept; it is the lineage's best).
  - Working keys and connections are lit ports: E20 lamps, breathing.
  - The live wire from OpenAI to the model box is lit phosphor.
  - Off ports are pewter rings (#8794a2), no longer blue.
- Words: title, lede, then one summary line that fills the space beside the tall figure: "3 of 4 answering · 1 key of 4 · $0.00 of $2.00 today". Each figure in it links to its plate.

Lamps plate: the legend figure (kept, now with glowing lamps), and the three columns with glowing lamps.

Cost plate: the figure is today's spend as a bar against the limit on the sheet, the spent part lit.

SETTINGS

Overview.
- Keep the exploded machine keyed 1-9 to the list.
- The part that needs a look is drawn amber; the rest is blueprint.
- Rows: the circled numeral, the title in ink 600 (no blue underline), the summary in --ink-2.

A section page (General).
- The machine's current callout is lit phosphor with its halo.
- "The parts" list shows the current part in steel reverse, with its ring lit.
- Fields follow the system. Save is the primary, in sentence case.

FORM (new idea)
- Keep the idea's anatomy drawing.
- The part being typed in lights phosphor with the halo. This is the parent's `:has()` device, now glowing.
- "Add it" is the primary and "Cancel" a secondary, both sentence case and 44px.

WISHES, MEMORY, FAMILY
- A figure only where there is data: a column per kid with a square per wish; on Family, the family's initials wired to Vera.
- Otherwise the plate spans.

SIGN IN AND 404
- The monitor with the face (E22) and power-on, in a thin case, beside the words.

PHONE (40rem and under)
- Top bar: the mark, then Memory, Family, Status and Settings as 44px icons.
- Bottom tab bar: six cells, each an icon over a sentence-case word, with the current one in steel reverse. No numerals.
- Every figure folds to a one-line summary strip in the Tab order. In `<details class="fig-fold">`, drop `tabindex=-1` from the summary and make it a 44px row, for example "Fig. 2 · 4 plans in four weeks · 2 late ▸". It opens to the drawing.
- The Next up monitor becomes a landscape strip under the question, never before it: radar 6rem at the left, words at the right, 9rem tall at most.
- Chat: the thread comes first.
briefs.borrows:
The judges' fixes, most cited first, with the lenses that asked for each:

1. Sentence-case Plex Sans buttons, nav, disclosures and see-more links, with mono caps tracked at .05em or less and kept for legends only. Type (r10, r11), system (r10, r11), interaction (r10, r11), usability (r11), skeptic (r10).
2. The paper "here" swapped for a steel reverse. Skeptic r10 asked for steel #748a9b and r11 for a steel reverse; feedback r11, soul r11, style r11 and system r11 all flagged the paper cells. The values #6e8496 with a #a9c4d8 cap come from the main lessons, rounds 8 and 11.
3. The lit glass pool round the ask box restored. System r10 fix (1), skeptic r10, soul r10 and r11, feedback r10. Built from kit E7, E1 and E4.
4. Row titles in ink, underlined on hover and focus only; blue underlines kept for prose and head links. Style r10, system r10 fix (2), type r10, skeptic r10, feedback r10 and r11.
5. Home shortened:
   - plates side by side at wide widths (type r10)
   - two columns at 1280 with To do on the first screen (usability r10)
   - one-line date rows of about 48px (interaction r10)
   - the tally beside To do (system r10 fix (5))
   - figure 1.4 folded into the setup list (interaction r10)
6. Targets of 44px or more. Interaction r10 and r11, usability r11.
7. Icons back in the phone tabs. Interaction r10, usability r10, skeptic r10, system r11, interaction r11.
8. CHAPTER numbering and section numbers dropped (usability r10, skeptic r10), with the FIG captions kept as sentence case (type r10).
9. Decorative figures dropped (the Plans key, Home's family tree), and the column collapsed where there is no real figure. System r10 fix (4).
10. Relative due dates and no italic caption. Type r10.
11. A speaker cue beyond shading, with the family on the right. Interaction r10, and the main lessons' round 10 open problem.
12. Phone figures as readable summary strips in the Tab order (style r10, interaction r10), and the radar shrunk on the phone (usability r10).
13. The empty band beside tall heads filled: the primary on the title row, a figure-summary line on Status, a narrower sticky figure column. Style r10.
14. "Let the lit figure glow like the original tube." Interaction r10, and soul r10's "unlit blueprint drawings".
15. A warm companion, put in the ink as bone rather than in a paper fill. Style r10.
16. Links retuned from #94bbfe to #9fb4d6. Style r11, lessons r11.

Small borrows, each answering a fault:
- L255, the amber tick box for late (r10-mut-4 Flight Deck, Lit), so late is never colour alone.
- The visible row afterglow values from L228 (r13-mut-3 Quote Board at Evening): a 12% steel wash, a 2px sage edge, 1.2s. This answers an open problem that has run five rounds.
- The thin 3px bezel, from the main lessons' round 13 open problem.

Kit effects used: E1, E2, E3, E4, E5, E6, E7, E9, E12 to E17, E19, E20, E22, and the Access blocks.
briefs.avoids:
It answers every fault the judges raised:
- Mono tracked caps on controls and links; the bar goes to sentence-case words with icons.
- The paper-grey glare; "here" becomes steel reverse, and the plate rules drop from light paper to pewter.
- The unlit greeting and the unlit blueprint figures, which cost it soul 5 and 5.4; the pool comes back, the monitors are at full strength, and each figure has one lit live mark.
- Every row as a blue underlined link.
- Home at 2437px with To do off the first screen.
- 14 and 20 small targets.
- Text-only phone tabs.
- CHAPTER and FIG costume.
- ISO dates.
- The italic caption.
- Decorative figures: the family tree and the Plans key.
- The one-sided desktop chat.
- The radar taking the Ideas phone screen.
- A cold, clever mood; bone ink and the lit pool warm it.

It also avoids the tournament's standing traps:
- amber with two jobs (today on the month becomes steel)
- an olive setup tray
- empty lit glass (tubes sized to their words)
- a thick pewter slab of a case
- a duplicate kind filter (the tally replaces the Kind select)
briefs.title: Tell Vera what to *plan*. An operator's manual speaks in instructions, and this is step one of the whole app: you tell her, and she plans it. It names FamilyDB's job (weekends and outings, the calendar, reminders, ideas worth keeping), names who does it, and invites a message in the family's voice. The key word lights where "mind" did. At 23 characters it fits one line on a 390px phone at 2rem condensed. It stays the box's label: , with {{ assistant }} in place of the name.

briefs.name: Live Figures
briefs.hypothesis:
The lineage's figures are its strength, but judges read them as unlit, printed and separate from the words. "FIG 1.2" was noise to read past, and the heads left an empty band beside tall drawings. Four grafted devices make every figure a live instrument joined to its rows:
- a round lit screen in every page head holding the page's one live number (Dessau Phosphor)
- figure marks that light when their row is pointed at, then fade like phosphor (Long Persistence)
- a caption that says how to read each figure, with a running lamp where it is live (Night Gallery)
- the whole manual set on one 24px baseline, which the drawing sheet's graph paper makes visible (Phosphor Blueprint)

This puts phosphor light on every page, exactly where data is live, which answers soul. It also gives the invisible row afterglow a place to show: the lit mark in the figure. The operator's manual stays recognisable at a glance: plates, the figure column, graph paper and chapter numbers.
briefs.brief:
Start from r10-wild-4. Copy variants/r10-wild-4 and keep it a clean sheet. Keep the manual: plates with a 2px rule (now #56615d), the figure column on graph paper, the hairline, figures drawn from data in blueprint (lines 1.25px #6f88b3, labels #9fb4d6), and the chapter numbers. Graft four features, each rebuilt in the lineage's blueprint-and-phosphor terms, and take the lineage's fixes with them.

FEATURE 1: L044, a round phosphor screen per page with its one live figure (GEM, from r13-wild-3 Dessau Phosphor)

It becomes each page head's figure.
- The head plate's figure column holds a round tube, 10rem across, sunk in the drawing sheet.
- Round it, on the sheet, a blueprint instrument ring: a 1.25px --draw circle 8px outside the glass, a tick every 15°, and a numbered scale where the figure has one.
- The case: a 3px graphite bezel #262c29 with a 1px #3a423e lip, and a power lamp at six o'clock.
- The glass: E13 and E14 (VT323, three halos, .35px blur, scanlines, sheen, falloff), with Dessau's dot-on warm-up.
- The figure is set by its length through container units (len-1 to len-6): a dim top word of at least 1.05rem, the big figure, and a small word under it.

It shows a figure the page does not already print:
- Home: the radar itself, round in round glass, with "17:00 TODAY" at the foot of the glass. Home's rectangular Next up monitor becomes this.
- Chat: her glyph screen at full size (E19) with "READY", or "WORKING" while a turn runs.
- Ideas: the map radar, home lit at the hub, with "NEAREST 18 MIN" at the foot.
- Plans, list and month: "NEXT IN 2 DAYS", through the macro's {'plan': entry} reading.
- To do: "2 LATE" in the amber tone (the tube's phosphor becomes #ffb850 with its own two-layer halo), or "NONE LATE" in green.
- Status: "SPENT TODAY $0.00 OF $2.00". The ring is drawn as a $0-$2.50 scale, with the spent arc lit, a lit limit tick at $2.00, and a ghost peak (the day's highest, else yesterday's) so $0.00 still reads.
- Settings: "PARTS 2 NEED A LOOK", amber while any do.
- Family: "PEOPLE 4". Wishes: "OPEN 0". Memory: "KEPT n".
- The form has none, since no glass is lit that is empty. Sign in and 404 keep their faced monitor.

briefs.avoids:
It answers the same faults as the refinement, by other means:
- Soul's "figures are unlit blueprint, little tube light outside the radar": there is a lit round instrument on every page head, running lamps in the captions, and marks that light.
- Usability's "FIG numbering is noise to read past": each caption now says how to read its figure.
- Style's empty space right of tall heads: the round screen is about the height of title and lede, and the tall drawings move to the first plate.
- The tracked-caps controls.
- The paper glare, replaced by a paper rail on a slate cell.
- The raw-HTML row links.
- The small targets.
- The text-only phone tabs.
- CHAPTER costume.
- ISO dates.
- The one-sided chat.
- The 2437px Home: 48px rows on the 24px rhythm, and setup beside wishes.

It also answers the tournament's open problems:
- Row afterglow invisible in stills for five rounds: the afterglow now shows in the figure's lit mark and the row's steel wash.
- A needle or gauge reading dead at $0.00: a limit tick and a ghost peak.
- A visible grid read as a teal wash: here it is confined to the drawing sheets.

It keeps a round screen only where there is a live figure, so no glass is lit that is empty. Amber has one job: the To do screen turns amber only for late. It imports none of the main line's defining structures: no cased terminal column, no listing bands, no cut plate, no big quote per section.
briefs.title: What's the *plan*? This is the question a family actually asks on a Saturday morning. It names FamilyDB's job in one word: weekends and outings, plans on the calendar, and the reminders and ideas that make them. It invites anything from "the hike on Saturday" to "remind me to book the campsite". At 16 characters it sits on one line on any phone, even at the 48px title step of the 24px grid. It keeps the refinement's key word, "plan", on purpose, so the judges compare only the voice (the family's question here, the manual's instruction there) with the light on the same word. It stays the box's label: .
